newsitem.title: FRANCE: Politician seeks Cr Foncier rethink.
newsitem.headline: Politician seeks Cr Foncier rethink.

text.p: A member of Prime Minister Alain Juppe's RPR Party called on Thursday for a rethink of plans to wind down property lending group Credit Foncier de France.
Deputy Jean-Jacques Guillet said the announcement that the government was breaking off the privatisation of regional bank CIC showed Juppe preferred pragmatism to dogmatism.
"Such pragmatism should also prevail in the case of Credit Foncier," Guillet said in a statement.
He highlighted that despite the massive losses of 10.8 billion francs and provisions of 13.6 billion francs written into the group's 1995 accounts, Credit Foncier had shown its abillity to recover.

The group reported a profit in the first half of 1996 but Finance Minister Jean Arthuis has already set a wind-down plan in motion. State bank Caisse des Depots has made an offer of 70 francs a share for the group on the state's behalf in the first stage of the wind-down process.
"It would also seem the right occasion to delay the dismantling given the institution's financial situation," Guillet said.
Arthuis, however, said on Thursday he was confident that the wind-down plan would go ahead according to plan.

Staff and trade unions have protested against the wind down, saying the group had indeed suffered from past mismanagement for which state officials were also partly to blame because of their involvement in management.
